newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says Germany to meet EMU criteria, timetable.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says Germany to meet EMU criteria, timetable.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Monday that he was sure that Germany would observe both the timetable and the entry criteria to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) on time in 1999.
Speaking after a meeting of his Christian Democrat (CDU) party leadership in Berlin, Kohl also said Germany would not allow a loose interpretation of the Maastricht treaty budget deficit target.
"The entry criterion of 3.0 percent (of gross domestic product) will not be watered down," Kohl told reporters.

Kohl's pledge to achieve a so-called "point-landing" on the Maastricht deficit goal follows heavy public pressure from Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber, a fellow conservative who has threatened to vote against joining EMU in parliament's upper house if the entry criteria are fudged.

Kohl, demonstratively backing embattled Finance Minister Theo Waigel, said his coalition government was steering a clear course towards the euro and added that he had "no doubt" that the single currency would be launched as planned in 1999.
He also said he saw good chances for economic growth to pick up to three percent in 1998. The government forecasts growth of 2.5 percent this year.
